summary_html: A **law-enforcement agency** encounters suspected maltreatment (e.g., during a domestic call or arrest) and **refers** to CPS. Federal child-abuse infrastructure promotes coordinated investigations via Children’s Advocacy Centers.
authority_html:

- **ASFA/SSA IV-E** — court findings and reasonable-efforts determinations later constrain downstream actions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: Sitting en banc in a case arising from the Wenatchee, Washington child sex abuse investigations, the court held there is no constitutional right to have child witnesses interviewed in a particular manner, and that a deliberate-fabrication claim requires evidence that investigators knew or should have known the accused was innocent or used techniques so coercive they knew would yield false information.
key_cases.relevance: Arose from a joint police and CPS investigation in Washington and defines the constitutional limits on that joint interviewing practice.
key_cases.quote: an allegation that an interviewer disbelieved an initial denial and continued with aggressive questioning of the child cannot, without more, support a deliberate-fabrication-of-evidence claim

key_cases.case_name: Miles v. Child Protective Services Department
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed dismissal of claims arising from an emergency removal, holding the caseworker was entitled to the good-faith immunity of RCW 26.44.056(3) where she relied on the opinions of treating physicians, and that the parents identified no clearly established constitutional right to support their section 1983 claim.
key_cases.relevance: Illustrates the joint hospital, law-enforcement and CPS pathway into protective custody and the immunity that attaches to it.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that a rational trier could not find causation, and that a rational trier would be obligated to find good faith.

key_cases.case_name: Rogers v. County of San Joaquin
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that warrantless removal of children is permissible only in cases of exigency, meaning reasonable cause to believe the child is likely to experience serious bodily harm in the time required to obtain a warrant, and reversed qualified immunity for the social worker because no reasonable social worker could have believed an exigency existed on this record.
key_cases.relevance: Applies the same exigency requirement to social workers and to the police officer who accompanied the removal, so a referral between them does not lower the constitutional threshold.
key_cases.quote: we hold that it was clearly established that warrantless removal of children is permissible only in cases of exigency
